segments.title: 第182章 同床
segments.content:
Reignited: The Green Days Chapter 182: Sharing a Bed

After searching on the computer for a long time, the three of them found *Interstellar*, which had just been released this year.

Originally, Li Luo thought the two girls would prefer to watch a romance film, but for these two top students, a sci-fi movie like *Interstellar* was probably more to their taste.

But then, another problem arose.

The three of them squeezing in front of the computer desk to watch a movie felt a little awkward.

Ying Chanxi glanced at Li Luo's bed and asked in a low voice, "Can we move the computer desk? It'd be more comfortable to watch lying on the bed, right?"

"You're quite demanding." Li Luo shot her a look. "Isn't sitting like this fine?"

"It is, but my back gets a little tired after sitting for so long." Ying Chanxi was sitting on a chair she had just brought in from the living room, and leaning against its back was definitely not as comfortable as being in a movie theater.

Li Luo was at a loss with her. He simply took out the laptop Yan Zhusheng had lent him before, got onto the bed with it, and said to the two, "Let's use this to watch then."

Ying Chanxi's eyes lit up, but she still feigned a moment of bashful reluctance.

But Xu Youyu, at the side, didn't mind at all. She went straight around to the other side of the bed and plopped down next to Li Luo.

Seeing this, Ying Chanxi quickly scrambled onto Li Luo's bed as well, a hint of regret in her heart.

She should have gotten on the bed earlier and asked her senior to sit next to her.

But what was done was done. Ying Chanxi was too embarrassed to say anything more. Just leaning against the headboard, half-lying down, was enough to make her cheeks flush.

Xu Youyu, on the other hand, had a completely normal expression. She even looked quite intrigued, excitedly lifting Li Luo's quilt and sliding her lower body underneath.

"Hehe, I used to dream about snuggling under the covers with friends to watch a movie. Today, that dream finally came true."

"Wait... Who said you could get in?" Li Luo looked at Xu Youyu's complete disregard for the propriety between men and women, utterly speechless.

But in the next second, Ying Chanxi on his right, not to be outdone, also slipped into the quilt.

Sandwiched between the two of them, Li Luo was suddenly unable to move.

Especially with the two girls having changed back into their pajamas, their charming and slender figures lying so close, Li Luo didn't dare to move.

"Let's watch the movie," Xu Youyu urged as she grabbed a bag of potato chips and tore it open.

Li Luo took a deep breath, opened Yan Zhusheng's laptop, found the stream for *Interstellar* again, and pressed play.

Ying Chanxi had already reached out and switched off the bedroom light.

"Why did you turn off the light?" Li Luo's eye twitched. He felt that something was not quite right.

But Ying Chanxi looked as if it were a matter of course. "Of course you have to turn off the lights to watch a movie, otherwise you can't see clearly."

By now, the opening credits of the movie had passed. Li Luo had no choice but to turn his head back and start watching the film with full concentration.

Xu Youyu and Ying Chanxi leaned against the headboard on either side of him, watching quietly with him.

Time passed just like that.

*Interstellar* was over two hours and forty minutes long. The three of them watched from midnight until past three in the morning.

Because Li Luo had already seen it once in his past life, he started getting drowsy midway through and simply closed his eyes and fell asleep.

When he seemed to have a realization in his sleep, sensing that something wasn't quite right, and then woke up with a start, Li Luo looked at the laptop on his legs, its screen long black, and then glanced at the clock on the wall...

It was already past five in the morning.

Li Luo dazedly turned his head, looking left and right, then held his forehead with a wry smile.

Xu Youyu and Ying Chanxi were both sleeping sweetly.

Xu Youyu's sleeping posture was particularly outrageous; one of her legs was draped directly over Li Luo.

Meanwhile, Ying Chanxi had a habit of unconsciously hogging the quilt in her sleep. As she slept, she had pulled it all over, leaving Xu Youyu with nothing to cover herself.

As a result, Xu Youyu had curled onto her side, pressing tightly against Li Luo, her brow slightly furrowed, clearly a little cold.

Li Luo took a deep breath, instantly wide awake. He sat up straight in bed and gently pushed Xu Youyu's leg aside.

Then, he slowly lifted the quilt, scooted his bottom along the bedsheet all the way to the foot of the bed, and finally managed to get off.

After finding and putting on his slippers, Li Luo had originally intended to just cover Xu Youyu with the quilt.

But fearing that Ying Chanxi would just snatch it away again, Li Luo simply went to Xu Youyu's bedroom, brought her quilt over, and covered her with it directly.

Once her body warmed up, the frown on Xu Youyu's sleeping face immediately smoothed out, and she fell into a deeper sleep.

Li Luo stood by the bed, looking at the two girls now lying on his bed, a helpless smile on his face.

This New Year's Eve was certainly quite unforgettable.

But he couldn't sleep in this bed anymore.

He had only managed to fall asleep last night because he was utterly exhausted. If he were to get back in between them now, he definitely wouldn't be able to sleep at all.

So Li Luo simply changed his clothes, grabbed his phone, walked out of the bedroom, closed the door behind him, and stretched in the living room.

Although he had only slept for a little over three hours, he felt quite energetic.

Li Luo thought for a moment, checked the time, and decided to just go downstairs for a morning run.

Just as he got down to the ground floor and stepped out of the elevator, his phone vibrated.

Li Luo thought it might be Xu Youyu or Ying Chanxi who had woken up.

But when he took out his phone, he saw it was a text message from Yan Zhusheng.

Yan Zhusheng: What's the earliest I can come over today?

Li Luo: Why are you awake so early?

Yan Zhusheng: You're awake too?

Li Luo: I'm going for a morning run.

Yan Zhusheng: Then can you wait for me at the school gate? I'll be right down.

Li Luo: You're not going back to sleep?

Yan Zhusheng: I've had enough sleep.

Li Luo: Alright then, I'll wait for you at the gate.

After texting Yan Zhusheng, Li Luo started walking towards the gate of the Fuyi High School dormitory campus while opening the Qidian Reading app.

As soon as he opened the software, the splash screen was an announcement for the joint interview event for *I'm Really Not a Star* with Yuan Wanqing.

Upon entering, the reader would be redirected to a reading event page.

The first thing to appear was an interview video.

And below the video were themed activities related to *I'm Really Not a Star*.

This included reading recommendations, subscription discounts, and a text version of the exciting content from the interview.

Li Luo raised his eyebrows, not expecting that he would ever get a Qidian splash screen feature in his lifetime.

You had to know, this was a spot generally reserved for only the most formidable top-tier authors.

For the Li Luo of his past life, it was something he could not even dream of.

And for the Li Luo of this life, although his new book's performance was good, based on the original circumstances, he was still some distance away from this spot.

But Li Luo would never have imagined that because of the song "Annual Rings," his book would be directly elevated to a height it didn't originally belong to.

In the words he had heard from a certain god-tier author in his past life:

Once the quality of a web novel reaches a certain level, the work's performance has little to do with the quality itself.

An 80-point web novel, given enough traffic, could very likely achieve much better results than a 90-point quality novel that wasn't appealing enough on its own.

This was pretty much Li Luo's current situation. If you asked him how amazing his book was, he himself didn't think so.

He had simply brought over the entire set of entertainment-genre tropes that had been summarized and categorized by numerous authors over a decade later.

In practice, it was just stringing a few main career plotlines together, then using various well-known music, film, and television works for plagiarism, allowing the protagonist to show off and slap faces, while also picking up some girls.

But as long as the quality was up to standard, without too many off-putting elements, ensuring that readers could continue reading after starting.

Then, when the traffic descended upon this book, the situation would spiral out of control.

Li Luo glanced at today's rankings, and his brows couldn't help but shoot up, his eyes filled with surprise.

*I'm Really Not a Star*

When a book that hadn't been seen much in the top ranks before suddenly appears on a chart like the bestseller list, it tends to attract readers' attention.

With the added boost from the splash screen feature, Li Luo shot upwards like a rocket.

But soon, Li Luo realized another factor.

He logged directly into Weibo and found Yuan Wanqing's Weibo account.

Just as expected.

From midnight until now, Yuan Wanqing's account had posted two updates.

One was a post about her participation in the Qianjiang Television New Year's Eve Gala, congratulating the successful conclusion of the gala.

The other was a repost of the Qidian interview event.

And compared to the congratulatory post linked with Qianjiang Television, the content of this repost seemed much more down-to-earth.

Yuan Wanqing: First thing I did after getting home from singing was to open my phone and start reading.

Below was a repost of the Qidian event for *I'm Really Not a Star*, which also included links to the Qidian Reading app and the Qidian website.

The comments below were also very interesting.

"No way, sis, you're in the entertainment industry and you read this kind of web novel too, hahaha."

"Why do I suddenly feel like Sister Qing has gone from an unapproachable goddess to the girl next door (lol)."

"Are you serious, sis? You actually read this book? Is it good?"

"The book is pretty good. That hit song of Sister Qing's, 'Annual Rings,' was originally written by this author."

"I'm gonna go check it out. I want to see what kind of book has Sister Qing so obsessed."

"Reporting in after reading all night. It's really good, damn it. Once you start, you can't stop. Good thing today's a holiday for New Year's Day. I'll sleep for a bit and then continue reading!"

Li Luo looked at this overwhelming flood of traffic and smiled faintly, thinking that his decision yesterday to release his hundred-thousand-word stockpile was absolutely correct.

This was also a major reason why *I'm Really Not a Star* could claim the top spot on the bestseller list.

After all, in this era, most authors weren't so hardcore, and releasing ten thousand words a day was not the norm.

At least for those already famous top-tier authors, releasing ten thousand words a day was a rare sight.

Now, with a "Reignited" suddenly emerging, it had caught many off guard.

In his comment section, readers who had stayed up all night reading had long since exploded.

"Bro, stop writing, I'm afraid I'll die from exhaustion if I keep reading!"

"Holy crap, are you trying to kill yourself? You're going this hard for an event?"

"Although I usually call you short and watery, your life is more important. Take a break, write again in the daytime."

"Wait, why do I feel like something's off? It's already four o'clock! Kid, are you posting from your stockpile?"

"A chapter every half hour? If you've got the guts, post for a whole day. I'd like to see if you can write faster than I can read."

Looking at the comments in his review section, Li Luo couldn't help but chuckle, finding them quite amusing.

By the time he was more or less done reading, he had already arrived at the gate of the Fuyi High School dormitory campus.

He didn't have to wait long before Yan Zhusheng, dressed in her school uniform, appeared in his line of sight, jogging over and quickly arriving in front of him.

"Good morning." Yan Zhusheng stopped and neatened her hair.

"Morning."

Li Luo watched as Yan Zhusheng raised both hands, gathered her long hair, and then skillfully tied it into a high ponytail with a hair tie from her wrist.

After she finished with her hair, Li Luo said, "Let's go, time to run."

"Okay." Yan Zhusheng nodded and fell into step with Li Luo, asking as she ran, "Was the promotion effective?"

"Better than I expected."

"Oh, that's good." Yan Zhusheng nodded. "The fireworks last night were beautiful."

"You are also very beautiful today."

"...Have you had breakfast?"

"Not yet."

"I want to eat xiaolongbao then."

"Alright, we'll go eat after our run."

"What about Xixi and my senior?"

"They're still sleeping. They went to bed pretty late last night, so they'll probably wake up very late."

"Oh."

Yan Zhusheng ran beside Li Luo, her figure slender, her steps light. Her ponytail swayed with her movement, brushing against her slim waist, and her eyes held a joyful smile.

"Li Luo, Happy New Year."

"Didn't we already say that yesterday?"

"It's better to say it in person."

"Well then... Happy New Year."

"Mhm."

(End of Chapter)
